title: Did Your AI Rollout Change Anything?
author: Magnetiz.ai
excerpt: Usage rises whenever people use the tool, whether the result moves or not. Playbook 10 names the one number a rollout is for, measures it before launch, and lets a rule signed in advance decide at day 30 whether to keep it, fix it or kill it.
content:
Name the number before the tool, and let the number decide.

The AI tool went live last quarter. People use it, the team says it saves time, and when someone asks what changed, the answer is a usage chart.

Usage is real. It answers a different question. Logins, drafts generated and seats activated rise whenever people use the tool, whether second meetings or speed to lead moved or not. A rollout judged on usage reads as done the day it ships.

Under that sits a second problem. Revenue numbers swing week to week with no tool at all. Without a baseline, one good week after launch looks like the tool working.

This week’s playbook handles both. Pick the one number the rollout is for, measure it for four weeks before launch, sign the keep, fix or kill rule while nobody has a stake in the result, and read it once on day 30.

Read the playbook →

The workflow, in seven steps

  1. Name the one number the rollout is for
  2. Measure four weeks before
  3. Write what counts as moved, and sign it
  4. Run it beside a holdout
  5. Log it every week
  6. Read it on day 30 against the signed rule
  7. Record the decision and start the next charter

The playbook page carries the reasoning for each step and flags the two places this most often goes wrong.

Two things the playbook covers in full

The rule you sign before launch. Why the owner of the number and the owner of the rollout both sign it before day one, and why the day 30 readout applies the rule instead of reopening it.

The five outcomes on day 30. Keep it, hold for 30 more days, fix it with one change, fix adoption or kill it, or keep recording because the count is too thin to call. The number, the holdout and usage together decide which one applies.

See the full workflow →

What is in the implementation kit

Six markdown files and the playbook PDF, free by email from the playbook page.

  • The one number charter, with the check that it is a result and not usage
  • The four-week baseline log
  • The rollout rule, signed before launch
  • The weekly log
  • The day 30 readout
  • A filled-in sample charter, from charter to decision

Start with the sample. Then write your own charter and rule before anyone touches the tool. If the owner of the number signs both, the setup is working.

One moved number earns the next test, never a pass for life.
